record.paper_title: On Plane Geometric Spanners: A Survey and Open Problems
record.original_question: In the constrained visibility-graph setting, where one is given a finite point set P and a noncrossing set L of constrained line segments and studies plane constrained spanners of the visibility graph VIS(P, L), determine the constrained analogues of the open questions from the unconstrained plane-spanner setting, since the constrained model generalizes the unconstrained one.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 21. Essentially, all of the questions that are open in the unconstrained setting are also open in the constrained setting since the constrained setting is a generalization of the unconstrained one.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let P be a finite set of points in the plane and let L be a finite set of line segments with endpoints in P such that no two segments of L cross in their interiors (a noncrossing constraint set). The visibility graph VIS(P, L) has vertex set P, and an edge uv whenever the open segment uv is not properly intersected by any segment of L (segments of L are themselves considered visible). A plane constrained spanner of VIS(P, L) is a planar subgraph G of VIS(P, L), containing L, whose Euclidean stretch factor relative to VIS(P, L) is bounded by a constant t; that is, for every edge uv of VIS(P, L), the shortest-path distance in G between u and v (using Euclidean edge weights) is at most t times the length |uv|.

Determine, in this constrained setting, the analogues of the principal open quantitative questions known for unconstrained plane spanners. Concretely:

(a) What is the smallest constant t for which, for every finite point set P and every noncrossing constraint set L, there exists a plane constrained t-spanner of VIS(P, L)?

(b) What is the smallest constant t for which, for every such (P, L), there exists a plane constrained t-spanner of VIS(P, L) of bounded maximum degree, and what is the minimum degree bound achievable simultaneously with a given t?

(c) Establish matching lower bounds (impossibility results) on t in (a) and (b).

The task is to settle these constants and tradeoffs, or to obtain improved upper and lower bounds beyond the currently known ones.
artifact.status_search_result: Research on plane constrained spanners of visibility graphs is active. Known results include that the constrained half-Θ₆-graph is a plane 2-spanner of VIS(P,L), the constrained Delaunay triangulation is a 2.42-spanner, and bounded-degree constructions exist with various stretch factors. However, the optimal stretch factor for plane constrained spanners and tight degree-stretch tradeoffs remain unresolved, mirroring the corresponding open problems in the unconstrained setting.

status_evidence.title: On Plane Constrained Bounded-Degree Spanners
status_evidence.snippet: The constrained half-θ₆-graph is a plane 2-spanner of the visibility graph Vis(P,S); a plane 6-spanner of Vis(P,S) with bounded degree can be constructed.
status_evidence.claim: Best known stretch factors and degree bounds in the constrained setting are still being improved, indicating the optimal constants remain open.

status_evidence.title: Routing on the Visibility Graph
status_evidence.snippet: Constrained Θ-graphs with at least 6 cones are spanners of Vis(P,S).
status_evidence.claim: Active investigation of stretch factors for constrained plane spanners continues.
